title: Stop committing compiled platform binaries to git -- build and publish from CI-qualified artifacts (supersedes QCLI-135)
description:
User decision, 2026-09-13, made via the orchestrator with the QCLI-135 trade-off stated explicitly (immutable human-inspectable git-committed artifact vs. a CI-built qualified artifact carried forward as a workflow artifact): converge npm/*/bin/ packaging on lore-cli's shape. Do not commit compiled platform binaries (npm/quest-*/bin/quest[.exe]) to git going forward. This is a deliberate supersession of QCLI-135's conclusion (which was correct when made, on 2026-08-30, under the constraints then understood), not a correction of it -- QCLI-135 stays Done and unedited; see its own added note recording the supersession.

Reference shape (this fleet's own working example, not a design to invent from scratch): lore-cli's .github/workflows/release.yml. Its `package-qualification` matrix job builds+packs+installs+smokes+audits each platform natively on its own runner, uploads the qualified tarball as a workflow artifact, and its `package` job re-verifies the tarball's sha256 against the qualification report before assembling dist-npm/ -- publish never re-reads a git-committed binary and never rebuilds between qualification and publish. lore-cli's npm/*/bin/ is gitignored; only npm/<platform>/package.json templates are committed.

quest-cli already has half of this pattern: .github/workflows/prepublication-qualification.yml's `immutable-candidates` job builds fresh per-platform (`bun run build:packages`) on non-release dispatches and uploads each as a `quest-package-<target>` artifact; its `candidate-bundle` job already downloads and reassembles those artifacts (see its chmod/executable-bit-restoration step, needed because artifact upload does not preserve file mode). What's missing is a path from a qualified artifact to `release.yml`'s `publish` job -- today that job's `npm publish` runs from a git checkout at the release tag, reading whatever is committed in npm/quest-<target>/bin/.

Constraints carried over from QCLI-135/QCLI-267 that the new shape must still satisfy, not relax:
- Bun's --compile output is not byte-reproducible. Whatever gets published must be the EXACT bytes that were qualified (native-execution receipt) -- never a fresh rebuild at publish time. lore-cli satisfies this by never rebuilding between its qualification and package jobs, only ever carrying the same artifact forward; the new quest-cli shape must do the same (carry `prepublication-qualification.yml`'s per-target build artifact through to `release.yml`'s publish job, not re-invoke `bun run build:packages` in the publish workflow).
- QCLI-267's release-provenance gate (scripts/qualification/release-provenance.mjs) checks the registry's gitHead against the SOURCE commit that was tagged/released -- this is about git HEAD identity, not file provenance, so it is unaffected by binaries no longer being tracked, but re-verify this explicitly rather than assuming.
- The native-execution receipt / --verify-committed path in prepublication-qualification.yml's immutable-candidates job is written around "the committed artifact is the thing being published" -- this needs to become "the qualified artifact from this run is the thing being published," which changes what --verify-committed verifies against (or replaces it with an artifact-identity check, mirroring lore-cli's sha256-against-qualification-report check in its `package` job).
- docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md documents the current procedure and will need updating to match.

Sequencing: this task is scoped and reviewed independently. It does not ride the chore/QCLI-271-release-0.6.1 branch, and QCLI-271's SIGKILL root-cause investigation proceeds independently -- the two may turn out to converge (once binaries are no longer tracked, the git operation that triggers the SIGKILL may simply never run again), but that would be a side effect to verify afterward, not a substitute for root-causing QCLI-271's blocker on its own.

The actual `npm publish` step remains in the fleet's irreversible set regardless of pipeline shape and goes to the user directly, never to an orchestrator.

acceptanceCriteria.text: npm/quest-*/bin/quest[.exe] are gitignored (npm/*/bin/, matching lore-cli), and are not present in any new commit going forward

release.yml publish job installs/publishes from a workflow artifact produced by prepublication-qualification.yml, not from a git checkout of committed binaries, and never re-invokes a build step between qualification and publish

The published bytes for each platform are provably the exact bytes the native-execution receipt qualified (an explicit identity check, e.g. sha256 comparison, mirroring lore-cli's package job), not merely bytes built from the same source commit
QCLI-267's release-provenance --pre/--post gates still pass unmodified in meaning (gitHead == released commit), re-verified against the new pipeline rather than assumed unaffected
docs/runbooks/quest-cli-package-and-release.md is updated to describe the new build-in-CI, never-commit procedure
QCLI-135 itself is left Done and unedited; the supersession is recorded as an added note on QCLI-135 referencing this task, date, and reason

implementationNotes: Cross-reference: the general host-level hazard this task's binaries are exposed to (any process that mmaps a signed macOS Mach-O built at a fixed path across repeated local builds can hit a stale kernel code-signing validation SIGKILL, per QCLI-271) is now documented fleet-wide by opum-doc: https://github.com/opum-ai/opum-doc/blob/main/docs/reference/native-macos-binary-git-sigkill-hazard.md (ODOC-188). Whatever build step lands in this task's new pipeline (CI build -> qualify -> artifact-carry -> publish) should write each platform binary to a fresh path/temp-then-rename rather than overwrite an existing output file in place, per that doc's general fix, even though moving off git-committed binaries independently reduces exposure to this specific symptom.

opum-cli-e2e (TASK-84, quest-cli workflow_dispatch run 34990618714, v0.7.1) found live evidence of exactly the divergence this task exists to close. The quest-candidate-bundle artifact win32-arm64 and win32-x64 tarballs are NOT byte-identical to what npm 0.7.1 serves: quest.exe is byte-identical, the file lists match, questBinarySha256 matches -- only package.json differs, by line ending (CRLF in the workflow-artifact build, LF in what npm serves). Root cause under the CURRENT dual-path architecture: the candidate bundle is assembled from immutable-candidates, which runs "bun run build:packages" fresh on each runner (including Windows) for a non-tag workflow_dispatch; a real tag release instead publishes the git-committed npm/quest-win32-*/package.json as-is (LF, as committed). Two different bytes, two different paths, same source commit. Reproduce: gh run download 34990618714 --repo opum-ai/quest-cli --name quest-candidate-bundle, then npm pack @opum-ai/quest-win32-x64@0.7.1, diff package/package.json. Nothing shipped 0.7.1 is wrong -- opum-cli-e2e is explicit this is a provenance-chain gap, not a product defect, and their own suite could not have caught it (compares bundle against its own manifest only; never a non-host candidate tarball against the registry -- filed as their own coverage-gap task). Cited here as concrete supporting evidence for this task, not a separate fix: it is a live instance of why "built from the same source commit" is insufficient, and AC#2/AC#3 (single artifact-flow path, explicit byte-identity check between qualified and published bytes) already covers closing exactly this gap -- the identity check should be byte-level (catches a text-file line-ending divergence too), not just sha256-of-binary.

Correction to the note above, from opum-cli-e2e plus independent re-verification here. The "build-fresh-on-Windows-runner vs git-committed-copy" framing overstated it: nothing was rebuilt. quest.exe is byte-identical across git HEAD at v0.7.1, the CI candidate bundle, and npm, for both win32 targets. Verified directly against the live run via `gh api repos/opum-ai/quest-cli/actions/runs/34990618714/jobs`: the "Run bun run build:packages" step is conclusion=skipped on both win32-x64 and win32-arm64 jobs (that run dispatched against the v0.7.1 tag ref, so the workflows if-condition that gates this step to non-tag refs correctly skipped it); "Attest the committed artifact" ran instead. build-platform-packages.mjs -- the only script that writes package.json -- therefore never executed on this run. So the CI bundles package.json is the SAME checked-out committed bytes, not a regenerated file; the divergence (CRLF, +21 bytes, otherwise identical content) has to be introduced between git checkout and artifact upload on the Windows runner, with no application code in between. The well-known mechanism for exactly this shape of corruption is Gits core.autocrlf defaulting to true on GitHub-hosted Windows runner images, silently rewriting a text files line endings on checkout; this is the best-supported explanation by elimination but has not been directly confirmed by reading that runners git config. Practical effect on this tasks design: this is not a build-reproducibility problem and collapsing the two pipelines is not what fixes it by itself -- the fix is controlling line-ending handling for text files on Windows checkouts (a .gitattributes rule such as "npm/**/package.json text eol=lf", or pinning core.autocrlf/core.eol in the workflows checkout step), independent of whatever artifact-flow redesign this task lands on. The byte-level, per-member identity check this tasks AC already calls for is still the right general safeguard and would have caught this regardless of root cause.

Further correction, read directly from release.yml rather than inferred: the publish jobs runs-on is ubuntu-24.04 for every platform, checks out once, and goes straight to "cd npm/quest-${target} && npm publish" with no build or regenerate step in between (its own comment: "nothing here rebuilds them"). So the publish path never touches a Windows runner and never regenerates package.json -- it ships the committed bytes unmodified, for every platform including win32. That directly rules out "publish path also saw a Windows checkout" and "publish emitted generated/regenerated bytes" as explanations for anything observed.

Two separate, now fully resolved findings, previously conflated as one:
(1) package.json (win32-arm64 + win32-x64): committed = LF, 446/440 bytes, 0 CR (git show v0.7.1:npm/quest-win32-*/package.json). Published npm bytes match the commit exactly (ubuntu checkout, no conversion). The CI qualification candidate-bundle copy is CRLF, 467/461 bytes, 21 CR -- and that job (immutable-candidates) DOES run natively on windows-2022/windows-11-arm for the win32 targets, with the build step confirmed skipped on this tag-ref run via the GitHub API. Checkout-time autocrlf on that Windows runner converting the committed LF file is now the only mechanism consistent with every measurement, not a hedge. Scope: qualification artifact only: nothing shipped is affected.
(2) LICENSE (win32-arm64 + win32-x64 only): CRLF, 1085 bytes, 21 CR, on EVERY path checked -- committed, CI bundle, and npm alike -- while the other four platforms LICENSE is LF, 1064 bytes, 0 CR. Confirmed via git log --follow --diff-filter=A that this file has been CRLF since the very first commit of the current history (a9fbc78, "Initial commit: fresh history after repository deletion/recreation", 2026-09-10) and has not changed since, through v0.6.1/v0.6.2/v0.7.1. This is a static, pre-existing content asymmetry baked into the git blob itself, not a runtime checkout artifact -- it looks identical on every path because nothing on any path ever rewrites it, not because the paths share a mechanism. Cosmetic, harms nobody, unrelated to (1); worth a one-line normalization commit whenever convenient but not urgent and not part of this tasks scope.

Net effect on this tasks design: unchanged from the prior note. Item (1) is a checkout-line-ending-handling fix (.gitattributes eol=lf or a checkout config pin for text files on Windows runners), orthogonal to the artifact-flow redesign. Item (2) is unrelated cleanup, mention only so a future reader does not reopen it as part of this investigation.

MERGED FROM QCLI-259 (same defect, earlier/investigative framing), 2026-09-17, during a fleet-wide dedupe pass. QCLI-259 established the current-state facts that led to this decision and is archived as a duplicate; its content preserved here rather than lost:

Filed while diagnosing QCLI-258s release-commit blocker (an OOM committing ~493MB of six platform binaries). Sizing at the time: current working trees npm/ (six 0.6.0 binaries) was 497MB; total .git was 1.0GB (208MB loose + 832MB packed) versus lore-clis 10.7MB (~55x smaller). Roughly half of quest-cli .git was the current versions binaries; the other roughly-equal half was superseded binaries from past releases (0.3.0 through 0.5.0) still sitting in packed history near original size, since compiled binaries do not delta-compress against each other -- every release compounds this, it is not one bloated commit. A history rewrite could recover several hundred MB but was explicitly out of scope, reserved for the users own direct authorization.

Mechanism established by reading release.yml, prepublication-qualification.yml, and native-execution-receipt.mjs directly: under the pre-QCLI-275 architecture, release.ymls Publish step does not rebuild -- it runs npm publish straight from npm/quest-${target} as committed at the release ref, gated by native-execution-receipt.mjs --verify-committed asserting git-blob equality plus a sha256 match. Buns --compile output is not byte-reproducible, so git-blob equality was the ONLY mechanism proving "the bytes CI attested to are the bytes that get published" (QCLI-135s fail-closed design) -- which is exactly the trust mechanism this task (QCLI-275) replaces with CI-artifact provenance instead.

Also carries a still-relevant compatibility note: a later correction from opum-agent recorded that a fresh native-execution receipt alone (produced at v0.6.0/ce551cf) did NOT flip opum-cli-e2es 6 stale-committed-receipt FAIL rows in its 50-packaging suite, because those rows read a hardcoded committed evidence path in opum-cli-e2es OWN repo unconditionally -- worth re-checking against opum-cli-e2e once this task ships, since the same class of stale-expectation mismatch could recur.
